variables.claim_asserts: Domestic dogs descend from several distinct wild canid species.
variables.test_measures: Whether each of 446 sampled dog mitochondrial CYTB+COX1 sequences is closer by ungapped p-distance to wild Canis lupus or to six other wild canid species.

modality.note: GenBank mitochondrial sequences are an appropriate ancestry modality, but they trace only maternal lineages and cannot exclude ancestry visible only in nuclear genomes.

assumptions.note: The nearest-reference-species comparison operationalizes distinct wild-species maternal ancestry; GenBank taxonomic labels are taken at face value, and no dog record has breed metadata.

scope.claim_scope: All ancestry of domestic dogs from wild Canidae.
scope.test_scope: Maternal ancestry represented by a systematic one-in-three sample of GenBank dog mitogenomes, compared with available wolf and six other canid species sequences.

reasons: The measured variable—0 of 446 dog mitogenomes having a nearest non-dog CYTB+COX1 sequence outside Canis lupus—directly probes multi-species maternal ancestry.
The interpretation explicitly states that mitochondrial DNA tests maternal ancestry only and that low-level non-wolf nuclear admixture is not excluded.
The zero-count refutation criterion is suitable for the tested maternal component, but it cannot by itself refute Darwin's unrestricted whole-genome descent claim.
what_would_change_it: Add representative nuclear whole-genome ancestry analyses across dog populations and the candidate wild canids; concordant absence of non-wolf ancestry would make the test faithful to the full claim.
